summary: Owner transcript lines 1-2700 of the LLM-Test session. The range opens mid-session (a compaction summary at L2, a second at L1888) and runs from committing the DIV_W/FAB_LR_OWN default changes through fifteen numbered pilot "rounds" on the owner's GPU box. The dominant activity is a loop: the assistant edits self_organize.py / longrun.sh in a container that has no GPU and (after a rebuild) no torch, pushes to branch rm-predict, hands the owner a single `git pull && ... bash longrun.sh ...` line, and the owner runs it on a rented Ubuntu GPU box and pastes back the grid summary plus uploaded .log files. The scientific arc: growth-off was proposed and reverted on the owner's objection; the ramp was found to starve the REGRESSION/stall growth triggers; identity collapse turned out to be already fixed at HEAD and FAB_EMB_VAR was found to *cause* it; mintok's apparent win was a per-token units artifact; the utilization cull gate was found shut in every run since FAB_N0=2048 landed (a regression the assistant introduced), fixed by FAB_PRESSURE=0.45; the GROW_CAP capacity valve was chased through five separate defects (two of them unit mismatches between flush-counts and step-counts) before it fired; a 0.75 GB / 8-epoch run and a 16-epoch run both failed, the latter blowing up at the epoch-2 LR peak. Specialization read INTERCHANGEABLE in every arm measured (up to 32). Every number below is n=1 or n=2 on 4-25 MB pilots against a measured replication floor of 0.039-0.131 b/B, so almost nothing in this range separates from noise.

levers.name: FAB_GROW
levers.effect: Master switch for fabric population growth. Set to 0 then reverted to 1 in this range.

levers.name: FAB_N0
levers.effect: Initial live expert count. Changed 3 -> 2048 in commit 6380519. Building the population beats ramping to it.

levers.name: FAB_NMAX
levers.effect: Hard preallocation ceiling for experts. Only preallocation — the real operating ceiling is FAB_PRESSURE x FAB_NMAX.

levers.name: FAB_RAMP_TO
levers.effect: Fraction of cap at which the population-building ramp latches off. Set to 0.5 so the ramp latches at step 1 and stops starving the REGRESSION/stall triggers.

levers.name: FAB_PRESSURE
levers.effect: Occupancy threshold gating the utilization cull route; behaves as a SETPOINT — population equilibrates at pressure x cap. Default changed 0.75 -> 0.45 (commit 8bf825f) on owner approval.

levers.name: FAB_PRESS_SOFT
levers.effect: New knob: judge occupancy against the GROW_CAP soft cap rather than FAB_NMAX. Built so option 3 could compete fairly; measured worse and later found to unpin the population (0.45 x 3000 = 1350).

levers.name: FAB_RESCUE
levers.effect: Mutate-instead-of-cull rate. Lives INSIDE the utilization-gated branch, so it is unreachable whenever occupancy < FAB_PRESSURE. Fired 203 times once the gate opened — first measurement since it was built 2026-08-14.

levers.name: FAB_KEY_NORM
levers.effect: Decides whether the HALT logit (and routing keys) is a raw dot product or a cosine over route_t. 0 -> HALT mass 0.0000 at depth 1.00; 1 -> HALT 0.9999 at depth 0.10. Controls HALT 4/4 but has no calibrated regime.

levers.name: FAB_EMB_VAR
levers.effect: Expert identity-embedding variance. The report advised raising it to fix collapse; measurement shows it CAUSES collapse — NN distance 0.1443 (1.0) -> 0.1166 (4.0) -> 0.0017 COLLAPSED (16.0), with held-out worsening monotonically 2.048 -> 2.109 -> 2.161.

levers.name: FAB_EC_W
levers.effect: Entry-logit deficit bonus. At 0.5 it restructured routing hard (1112 experts vs 674, top-share 4.4% vs 6.8%) without moving specialization.

levers.name: DIV_W
levers.effect: Expert distinctness reward. Default changed 0.0 -> 0.02 (commit 0809563) on n=1 evidence at the replication floor; the comment records it as a placeholder to be re-tested.

levers.name: FAB_LR_OWN
levers.effect: Per-expert LR clone. Default changed 1 -> 0 (commit 0809563); measured effect 0.0040 and it explains the flat FAB_LR_CYCLE ladder; turning it off saves a ~50MB per-step clone.

levers.name: GROW_CAP
levers.effect: Master switch for the soft capacity valve (both experts and vocabulary). Defaults to 0 and had never run before this range. Lifts only when the cap is BOTH pinned AND the loss has plateaued.

levers.name: GROW_CAP_FAB0 / GROW_CAP_VOCAB0
levers.effect: Soft starting caps. CRITICAL: the expert soft cap must sit AT OR BELOW the cull settling point (FAB_PRESSURE x FAB_NMAX) or the population never pins and the valve is dead.

levers.name: GROW_LIFT
levers.effect: Size of each cap lift. Was a MULTIPLIER of 2.0 (runaway), changed to a flat count of 256 at owner instruction, then changed again to a FRACTION of 0.08 at owner instruction, with GROW_LIFT_MIN=8 as an absolute floor.

levers.name: GROW_CAP_EVERY
levers.effect: Minimum interval between lifts. Semantics changed from steps-since-last-lift to STEPS-PINNED; default 2000 -> 20000. Was compared against a flush-count clock twice (two separate unit bugs).

levers.name: GROW_CAP_PLATEAU
levers.effect: Improvement threshold below which the loss counts as stalled (default 0.002). The gate was `improving < PLATEAU`, which admits every negative value — i.e. a run getting worse read as a stall. Changed to a two-sided band.

levers.name: PLATEAU_WARM
levers.effect: New constant (1000, deliberately NOT a knob): number of slow-EMA observations before 'not improving' is a reading rather than an initialisation. Replaces the misused GROW_CAP_EVERY warmup gate.

levers.name: LOSS_MASK_DEAD
levers.effect: Excludes unminted vocabulary rows from the softmax denominator. MANDATORY for the vocabulary half of GROW_CAP — without it the run measures the reservation, not the mechanism. Measured ALONE it is the worst arm of round4 (+1.353).

levers.name: VMAX
levers.effect: Fixes the softmax width at startup; the vocabulary grows into it by minting. It is a CEILING, not something that expands — it saturated at 2048 on a ~70k-step pilot. Vocabulary size is the largest single lever measured (0.141-0.205 b/B).

levers.name: TOK_MINT_UNTIL
levers.effect: Freezes vocabulary MINTING (sets _mint_frozen, gating pair tallying and TOK.maybe_grow). Does NOT freeze embedding learning and does NOT freeze segmentation. Measured a dead heat against base on d_order1.

levers.name: RETOK_EVERY
levers.effect: Re-segmentation cadence (3000). Independent of TOK_MINT_UNTIL — a frozen arm still pays a retok tax and still has fabric growth periodically blacked out, for no benefit.

levers.name: SELF_ORG
levers.effect: Domain self-assembly. SELF_ORG=0 is the no-domains lever, but it also collapses MEM_OWNERS to 1 unless MEM_PER_EXPERT=1 — so it is 'no partition at all', not 'partition by expert'.

levers.name: MEM_PER_EXPERT
levers.effect: Partitions the memory store by expert. Defaults to 0 (assistant twice stated otherwise). Recorded cost at its own read site: global 200k slots -> memory contributes -0.097 b/B; 32 owners x 64 -> -0.652 b/B. It once made a faded domain vanish entirely.

levers.name: MEM_OWNERS
levers.effect: Number of memory ownership buckets (64). Ownership is `own % n_own`, so at 2048 experts 32 experts share each partition — it is per-64-buckets memory, not per-expert.

levers.name: BEST_KEEP / BEST_KEEP_TOL
levers.effect: New: retains the n most recent local lows as .best1..bestN, rotating, gated on being within BEST_KEEP_TOL (2%) of the best so far. Implements the owner's 'checkpoint every local low point'. Defaults to 0 — must be set explicitly. Rule is really 'a descent into a good region', a superset of true local minima.

levers.name: LR_EPOCHS
levers.effect: Cosine wavelength in epochs. LR_EPOCHS=0 (span all epochs) was the assistant's recommendation and broke round13 by holding the LR near peak across the epoch-2 resample shock.

levers.name: LR_STEPS
levers.effect: New knob (default 0, schedule bit-identical when unset): states the cosine wavelength directly in steps, skipping the epoch projection entirely. Built at owner instruction after 'LR_EPOCHS=8' meant 48,000 steps in one run and 840,000 in another.

levers.name: LR_SHIFT_WARM
levers.effect: New knob (default 0): attenuates the cosine for N steps after note_shift() marks our own distribution change (retok / epoch resample / LR restart). Multiplicative so it can only lower the rate, never raise it mid-anneal.

levers.name: STREAM_LEN
levers.effect: Bytes per epoch. Owner fixed it at 94000000 for the 0.75 GB run (94 MB x 8 epochs) and later ran pilots at 25000000. This is the number that makes 'EPOCHS=8' mean anything.

levers.name: BATCH_W
levers.effect: Windows per flush (16). Everything below the batch early-out runs once per FLUSH while `step` advances once per WINDOW — the source of two separate 16x unit-mismatch bugs in the capacity valve.

levers.name: FABRIC
levers.effect: Master fabric switch. FABRIC=0 crashed on an unguarded `_F0.div_mass` in the _EFF banner list; now covered by a static check in levers.py.

levers.name: GRID_DIR / PAIR_DIR / SEEDS / DEVICE
levers.effect: longrun.sh harness controls: output directory (used to keep rounds from overwriting each other), seed list for paired arms, and device selection. Owner set DEVICE=cuda explicitly from round11.

carry_forward.item: When an instruction of the owner's is being reversed by new evidence, say so explicitly rather than switching quietly. The GROW_LIFT fraction change was flagged as reversing the owner's own 'linear, not percentage' instruction, with the reason the original instruction had been right about the case it addressed.
carry_forward.why: Keeps the owner's model of the system accurate and preserves the audit trail of why an instruction stopped applying.

carry_forward.item: FAB_PRESSURE is a SETPOINT, not a threshold: the expert population equilibrates at FAB_PRESSURE x cap. Predicted 1843, measured 1838; predicted 3686, lr_novalve measured 3932. FAB_NMAX is preallocation, not the operating ceiling.
carry_forward.why: Every capacity decision downstream depends on this — the cull gate, the valve's eligibility window, and whether a soft cap can ever pin.

carry_forward.item: The GROW_CAP expert valve can only fire if GROW_CAP_FAB0 sits AT OR BELOW the cull settling point (FAB_PRESSURE x FAB_NMAX). Above it the population settles below the soft cap, is never pinned, and the valve correctly declines forever. This killed the valve in round6 and would have killed it in the 0.75 GB run.
carry_forward.why: It is the single arithmetic relation that decides whether the owner's 'pressure valve' exists at runtime, and its failure mode (silence) is indistinguishable from 'never plateaued'.

carry_forward.item: The vocabulary valve and the expert valve are structurally asymmetric: minting refills the vocabulary within a few steps so it re-pins immediately, while expert growth comes only from rare REGRESSION/stall bursts so the population never refills to a lifted cap. One GROW_LIFT knob serving both is a known mismatch.
carry_forward.why: Explains why the vocabulary lifted 6-19 times while experts lifted 0-5 in every measurement, and why an over-eager vocabulary valve is the mechanism that spent the 0.75 GB run.

carry_forward.item: Everything below the batch early-out (`if len(_bx) < BATCH_W: step += 1; continue`) runs once per FLUSH while `step` advances once per WINDOW. Any counter or cadence written there is 1/BATCH_W of what its name says. This produced two independent 16x unit bugs in the same mechanism.
carry_forward.why: The file already warns that modulo cadences down there fire ZERO times, which is loud; a +1-per-call clock fires at the wrong RATE, which reads as the mechanism declining on the merits.

carry_forward.item: `d_order1` (= order1 - held_out) is a MARGIN — higher is better — and it is the only cross-corpus-comparable column. `held_out` is not comparable whenever the order-1 anchors differ, which happens whenever the corpus is re-fetched or the vocabulary policy changes the bytes covered by a fixed step budget.
carry_forward.why: compare.py had this backwards and routed users onto the metric it got wrong exactly when they could not eyeball the answer. Two grids were nearly misread on held_out alone.

carry_forward.item: `since the minimum` in a log is per-TOKEN cross-entropy and rises mechanically as minted tokens carry more bytes. The unit-stable figure is the `UNIT-STABLE CROSS-CHECK (held-out bits/byte)` line three lines below it, which the log itself annotates 'Judge this run on bits/byte.'
carry_forward.why: An entire session's worth of conclusions was drawn from the wrong one of two adjacent lines, and the grid summary was surfacing the misleading number while hiding the correct one.

carry_forward.item: Measured noise floors at pilot scale: unpaired replication floor ~0.039 b/B (older regime); seed spread on d_order1 measured 0.066-0.131 this session; two runs with identical flags and no behavioural code change landed 0.066 apart. Pairing collapses the floor a lot (compare_test: per-arm spread 0.456/0.384 vs paired 0.113).
carry_forward.why: The four best arms in the project sit inside 0.06 b/B of each other, so nearly every single-arm difference reported in this range is inside noise and must be labelled as such.
carry_forward.evidence: assistant at jsonl:714, :2327; owner-pasted seeds summary at jsonl:719

carry_forward.item: Judge structural interventions on DID IT FIRE, not on bits/byte, and commit to that before seeing the numbers. 'An arm that changes nothing AND never fires is a different finding from one that fires and changes nothing — only the second is about the idea.'
carry_forward.why: Round5 was decided correctly this way; round4's `rescue` arm was misread as evidence about the idea when it was evidence about the configuration.

carry_forward.item: 'Unreachable' is not the same as 'inert', and the audit must distinguish them — they have different fixes. A mechanism reported as ARMED AND INERT when the run simply never asked reads as 'the idea does not work'.
carry_forward.why: This misreading is what let the shut cull gate survive an entire round, and it is the central discipline of the DID IT FIRE audit.

carry_forward.item: Never infer coverage from a config file — infer it from a log. `nofabric` was in GRID_ARMS_DEFAULT, which was taken as proof the FABRIC=0 path had run; that list had never been run and the crash was real.
carry_forward.why: It cost a grid arm and it is the exact reasoning error the DID IT FIRE audit exists to prevent.

carry_forward.item: Pure arithmetic used by the training loop must be hoisted to module level and tested by loading it from the shipped source (by AST, not by importing self_organize), so the test exercises the real text and still runs when torch is missing. proj_arith, lift_to, and the ramp latch are all covered this way; proj/cap/ramp/lr tests run torch-free.
carry_forward.why: This arithmetic has been wrong twice in opposite directions in the same knob, and the assistant's container has no torch, so a torch-dependent test would be unrunnable exactly when it is needed.

carry_forward.item: A report bug must never be able to destroy a finished run. `_keep` killed a completed 60,227-step arm in a print; the block is now wrapped, and on an 11-hour job that fault would have cost the whole run.
carry_forward.why: Long runs are the expensive resource; a summary line is not.

carry_forward.item: The 8-epoch cosine wavelength survives the epoch-2 resample shock and a 16-epoch one does not. Both runs take the shock at the boundary; the difference is that an 8-epoch schedule is at 19% of peak by the fifth boundary while a 16-epoch one is still at 50%. Prefer LR_STEPS (absolute) over LR_EPOCHS (corpus-dependent, 17x range observed).
carry_forward.why: This is the only identified cause of a catastrophic, unrecovered blow-up in this range, and it was caused by an assistant recommendation.

carry_forward.item: On pure language quality the fabric is a wash: nofabric ties pop1024 within noise (0.061 vs a 0.066-0.131 spread), because the fabric makes the base model 0.285 b/B WORSE standalone and then hands back roughly what it took. SUFFICIENCY says 479 experts buy -0.002 over the best single rank-slot. The fabric therefore earns its keep ONLY on continual learning — and the eng -> add py -> eng chain has still never been run.
carry_forward.why: This is the load-bearing open question for the whole architecture, and every single-corpus pilot in this range is structurally incapable of answering it.

carry_forward.item: Specialization has read INTERCHANGEABLE in every arm ever measured (32 by the end of this range), across DIV_W at three settings, FAB_KEY_NORM, FAB_EMB_VAR at three, frozen vocabulary, domains off, FAB_EC_W, and every population size 128-4103. Load-spreading and competence-differentiation are unrelated in this system.
carry_forward.why: Any future intervention aimed at differentiation must be measured against this baseline, and no intervention tried so far has moved it.

carry_forward.item: Vocabulary SIZE is the largest quality lever measured at pilot scale (0.141-0.205 b/B), and it moves the wrong way — every run ending near 2048 tokens scored ~2.0-2.18, both runs past 4800 landed ~2.3, at 4 MB and 94 MB alike. carry_forward.item: TOK_MINT_UNTIL freezes MINTING only — not embeddings (no requires_grad=False or .detach() anywhere near embeddings, delta, dbias or the head) and not SEGMENTATION (RETOK_EVERY keeps re-segmenting, clearing the lookahead queue and blacking out fabric growth). RETOK_EVERY=0 is a separate knob and neither implies the other.
carry_forward.why: The owner explicitly worried that freezing would stop token embedding learning; it does not, but a frozen arm still pays a retok tax for no benefit, which is what frozen_nr exists to measure.

carry_forward.item: BEST_KEEP implements 'checkpoint every local low point' as 'a descent into a good region' — a superset containing every local minimum plus points on the way down — because a true local minimum can only be confirmed one probe after the weights have moved past it. Defaults to 0; must be set explicitly. Estimated ~420-515 save events over a long run rotating through n resident slots, so n is a disk budget, not a coverage decision.
carry_forward.why: The owner asked for local-minimum checkpointing specifically; this records what was actually built and why it deliberately over-saves.

carry_forward.item: Per-expert memory (MEM_PER_EXPERT=1) is off by default for a recorded reason and is a retest of a known-bad configuration: it once made a faded domain vanish entirely (every English entry evicted, the unlearn test skipped as vacuous) because owners are experts folded mod MEM_OWNERS and eviction inside a block was LRU on WRITE-recency. The eviction-clock work (last-retrieval + read probe) repaired it — round3's nodom_mem drift was +0.015 against base +0.010 — but only on a single stationary corpus.
carry_forward.why: Read nodom_mem on the retention section, never on bits/byte, and treat the repair as unproven under a real domain switch.
